_note: Tranche 2 round 2, corrected after round 1 (6 fetched, 6 failed). Nothing here has been downloaded. Every url, expected_producer and expected_bytes remains an expectation, not a measurement; fetch_expansion.py records what arrives and reports divergences. Round 1 evidence drives this list: nvlpubs.nist.gov went 3/3 and irs.gov 2/2, so the reliable hosts are weighted heavily. Candidates already sealed are absent. Licences are restricted to US Government works and CC-BY/CC0; arXiv remains excluded because its default submission licence does not grant onward redistribution.

_round_1_failures.D11a_crs_403: crsreports.congress.gov returned 403 Forbidden to a declared non-browser User-Agent. NOT retried and the UA is NOT disguised: defeating a bot filter by impersonating a browser is evasion. Replaced by D11b, the same public-domain CRS work from EveryCRSReport, which publishes an open bulk access policy.
_round_1_failures.D19a_D19b_D20a_rfc_404: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfcNNNN.pdf 404s for these three. That path serves a native PDF only for RFCs authored in RFCXML v3 (roughly 2019 onward); 8259 (2017), 2119 (1997) and 793 (1981) predate it. The RFC Editor publishes generated PDFs of older text RFCs at /rfc/pdfrfc/rfcNNNN.txt.pdf, which is the corrected path below. D19c adds a modern RFC to exercise the native-PDF form as well.
_round_1_failures.D26a_ecb_ssl: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED (unable to get local issuer) on Windows: the system store populates intermediates lazily via CryptoAPI and Python does not drive that. Fixed in fetch_expansion.py by preferring certifi's bundle. The ECB URL itself was also an unverified guess and is dropped in favour of hosts whose paths are easier to confirm.
_round_1_failures.D32a_wikimedia_429: Rate limited. fetch_expansion.py now honours Retry-After exactly once. Retained below.
